title: Locusts
lead: The insects of the eighth plague of Egypt, a curse of the covenant, and the image of an invading army. Joel is the Bible's book of locusts, with four Hebrew names for them.

sections.b: Locusts (Hebrew 'arbeh) were eaten as food (Leviticus 11:21-22) and feared as a plague. They are the eighth plague of Egypt (Exodus 10:1-20), one of the curses for breaking the covenant (Deuteronomy 28:38, 42), a trouble for which Solomon asks the LORD's help (1 Kings 8:37) and the picture of an army that has no number (Judges 6:5; 7:12; Jeremiah 46:23). John the Baptist ate them (Mark 1:6), and in Revelation 9:1-11 they come from the abyss.
sections.refs: Leviticus 11:21-22; Exodus 10:12-15; Deuteronomy 28:38; 1 Kings 8:37; Judges 6:5; Mark 1:6; Revelation 9:1-11

sections.b: The Bible has about nine Hebrew words for locusts and grasshoppers. Joel uses four in a row (gazam, 'arbeh, yeleq, chasil, Joel 1:4; 2:25). Others are sol'am and chargol (Leviticus 11:22) and gov (Amos 7:1; Nahum 3:17). Which insect each names is uncertain, and several may be stages of growth or kinds of the desert locust.
